root_cause.text: The imx8m-blk-ctrl driver incorrectly modeled i.MX8MQ VPU subdomains G1/G2 as having independent reset and clock control via rst_mask/clk_mask, even though the VPUMIX ADB hardware resets and ungates them only together, causing invalid separate resets that can hang the system.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and added comment explicitly state that “the ADB in the VPUMIX domain has no separate reset and clock enable bits” and that “we can't reset G1 or G2 separately, it may led to the system hang,” and the patch fixes this by removing `.rst_mask` and `.clk_mask` from `imx8mq_vpu_blk_ctl_domain_data` for `IMX8MQ_VPUBLK_PD_G1` and `IMX8MQ_VPUBLK_PD_G2`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop applying separate G1/G2 reset and clock masks on i.MX8MQ VPU domains and let the VPU power notifier handle reset sequencing to prevent system hangs.
intent_record.what: A comment block was added above imx8mq_vpu_blk_ctl_domain_data[] explaining i.MX8MQ VPU reset/clock behavior, and the rst_mask and clk_mask field initializers were removed from the G1 and G2 entries of that domain data array.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the G1 and G2 VPU subdomains will no longer use their per-domain reset and clock mask settings from the domain data, avoiding separate resets/clocks for those blocks and relying instead on imx8mq_vpu_power_notifier() to perform the VPU reset handling; this prevents hangs caused by resetting G1 or G2 independently.

grouping_result.intent: Stop applying separate G1/G2 reset and clock masks on i.MX8MQ VPU domains and let the VPU power notifier handle reset sequencing to prevent system hangs.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly removes the incorrect independent G1/G2 reset/clock mask handling on i.MX8MQ VPU domains and relies on shared notifier-based reset sequencing, which matches the root cause of invalid separate resets causing hangs.

candidates.rationale: This models the G1 subdomain as having its own independently controllable reset bit, which is the core incorrect assumption; the hardware resets G1/G2 together, so using a separate reset mask can trigger invalid reset sequencing and hangs.

This models the G1 subdomain as having its own independent clock ungate/control bit, contrary to the hardware behavior where G1/G2 are ungated together through VPUMIX ADB, contributing to invalid separate power-control operations.

This models the G2 subdomain as independently resettable, which is directly inconsistent with the actual shared reset behavior of G1/G2 and can cause the bad reset operations described in the root cause.
This models the G2 subdomain as independently clock-controlled, matching the same faulty assumption as the separate reset mask and enabling unsupported per-domain control that can hang the system.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line incorrectly models the i.MX8MQ VPU G1 subdomain as having an independently controllable reset bit. The root cause states G1/G2 are actually reset together by VPUMIX ADB, so this separate reset mask enables invalid reset sequencing that can hang the system.

This line incorrectly models the G1 subdomain as having independent clock control. Since the hardware ungates G1/G2 together, this per-domain clock mask contributes to unsupported separate control operations tied to the vulnerability.

This line incorrectly models the i.MX8MQ VPU G2 subdomain as independently resettable. That conflicts with the shared G1/G2 reset behavior described in the root cause and allows the invalid separate resets that can hang the system.

This line incorrectly models the G2 subdomain as independently clock-controlled. Because G1/G2 are ungated together in hardware, this mask encodes the same faulty assumption and enables unsafe per-domain control.

soc: imx: imx8m-blk-ctrl: add i.MX8MQ VPU blk-ctrl

This adds the necessary bits to drive the VPU blk-ctrl on the i.MX8M
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it directly shows how the i.MX8MQ VPU subdomains G1 and G2 are modeled in the domain data table. The root cause says the bug is modeling G1/G2 as having independent reset/clock control via `rst_mask`/`clk_mask`, even though hardware controls them together. That vulnerable construct is present here: for `IMX8MQ_VPUBLK_PD_G1`, the code assigns `.rst_mask = BIT(1)` and `.clk_mask = BIT(1)`; for `IMX8MQ_VPUBLK_PD_G2`, it assigns `.rst_mask = BIT(0)` and `.clk_mask = BIT(0)`. These per-domain independent masks explicitly encode separate reset/clock handling for G1 and G2. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present. The fix is not present, because the table still contains the independent `rst_mask`/`clk_mask` assignments instead of removing or otherwise correcting them to reflect the shared hardware behavior.
